title: Short Stuff: La Pascualita
summary: Short Stuff episode on La Pascualita, a long-standing bridal shop mannequin in Chihuahua, Mexico, that many locals believe is an embalmed corpse of a bride-to-be from the 1930s. The hosts walk through the urban legend (versions of the daughter's death, the mother's supposed embalming), the shop's owner Pasquala Esparza, and the research by Teresa Cordova that found no record of a daughter. They explain why embalmers say a corpse could not look this way after decades in a sunny window, compare it to Lenin's preserved body, note the unverified varicose veins claim, and close by wondering who made the mannequin.

segments.title: Introduction to La Pascualita
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the urban legend of La Pascualita, a bridal shop mannequin in Chihuahua that has stood since the 1930s and that many believe is an embalmed corpse.

segments.title: The corpse bride legend
segments.summary: The hosts recount the legend: a bride-to-be died in the 1930s (versions cite a broken heart or a black widow bite), and her mother had her embalmed and placed in the shop window. The owner is named as Pasquala Esparza.

segments.title: No daughter found
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a picture comparing the daughter with the mannequin. Teresa Cordova's 2012 University of New Mexico dissertation found no record of a daughter, the shop manager canceled an interview, and the hosts suspect the publicity is a marketing tool.

segments.title: Could it be a real embalmed body?
segments.summary: Embalmers consulted via Reddit and funeral industry sources say no embalming would last this long in a sunny window. The hosts compare it to Lenin's preserved body, which is kept under strict conditions and has been restored over the years.

segments.title: Varicose veins claim and the mannequin's origin
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the unverified claim that the figure has varicose veins, attributed to an unnamed former shop worker who may not exist, and the dress-changing curtain rule. They note no one has identified the mannequin's manufacturer, and that the mystery helps keep the legend alive.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh closes the episode, and the hosts sit in silence for thirty seconds before the sign-off and iHeartRadio production credit.
